# Research leads

A lead is an idea, question or source worth following that is not yet a task. Each one says how sure we are of it
(the tier of its best source), what data it needs and what that source permits, how any public sentence from it would be
grounded, and what it must not be used to claim. A lead becomes a `proposed` row on the lab's task board only when
someone writes that row; only a person sets a row `ready`. How to add, update or drop a lead: [README.md](README.md).

Tiers: T0 a summary or memory, unverified; T1 a quote from a primary source with its id and date; T2 T1 plus a script
check and a different model's check; T3 T2 plus a person's review. Effort is an estimate.

## Idea

### L-0002 Results posted, and registry records linked to publications by exact trial-id match

- **Question:** For CF trials in the registry, how many have results posted, and how many have a publication that cites their trial id exactly?
- **Why it matters:** Researchers and clinicians weigh evidence differently when they know how much of the registered trial record reached results or a paper.
- **Sources:**
  - T0, literature, not read by us. a published study of registry-to-publication links found in the 2026-10-10 literature search; citation to be recorded: Agent-read abstract, not re-read here: about 23.2 percent of trials had a direct registry-to-PubMed link and about 44 percent of the apparently unlinked had a paper when searched by hand. Both figures are T0.
  - T0, council, not read by us. three blind council reviews of the atlas, 2026-10-10: Suggested as a follow-on view.
- **Data:** clinicaltrials-gov, europe-pmc, ncbi-eutils (api); already have: no; fields missing: publication links by trial id (Europe PMC or PubMed search)
- **Effort:** M (estimate)
- **Guard:** computed, lab-position. An exact trial-id match gives a lower bound only, and every count says so in the same sentence.
- **Must not claim:**
  - That a trial without a matched paper is unpublished.
  - That a match rate measures a sponsor's conduct.
- **Needs a person:** maintainer-approval
- **Links:** none
- **Recorded:** created 2026-10-10 by model (claude-opus-5-5); updated 2026-10-10

### L-0004 Registered outcomes before and after CFTR modulator approvals

- **Question:** Did the mix of registered primary outcomes in CF trials shift between the eras around each modulator approval?
- **Why it matters:** Trial designers and clinicians may want to see how registered endpoints changed as modulators changed care.
- **Sources:**
  - T0, council, not read by us. three blind council reviews of the atlas, 2026-10-10: Start dates with no date type are shown as a band, not placed in an era.
- **Data:** clinicaltrials-gov, openfda-drugsfda (api); already have: no; fields missing: US approval dates from openFDA Drugs@FDA
- **Effort:** M (estimate)
- **Guard:** computed, lab-position. Era counts are computed; approval dates come from openFDA records; the framing is labelled a lab position.
- **Must not claim:**
  - That an approval caused any change in what trials register (no causal words).
  - That a start date with no date type belongs to a particular era.
- **Needs a person:** clinician-reader
- **Links:** none
- **Recorded:** created 2026-10-10 by model (claude-opus-5-5); updated 2026-10-10

### L-0005 Embeddings and seeded clustering as an internal aid for finding lexicon terms

- **Question:** Can embeddings with clusters seeded by the existing lexicon classes surface outcome wording the lexicon misses?
- **Why it matters:** A better lexicon sorts more outcomes by rule, so fewer depend on a model's proposal.
- **Sources:**
  - T0, council, not read by us. three blind council reviews of the atlas, 2026-10-10: A local embedding model is not yet onboarded; it would go through the model-onboarding checklist first.
- **Data:** clinicaltrials-gov (api); already have: yes; fields missing: none
- **Effort:** M (estimate)
- **Guard:** lab-position. Internal only: a cluster suggests terms for a person to add as rules; clusters never publish.
- **Must not claim:**
  - That a cluster is a category of outcome.
  - Any count or figure from clusters.
- **Needs a person:** maintainer-approval
- **Links:** none
- **Recorded:** created 2026-10-10 by model (claude-opus-5-5); updated 2026-10-10

### L-0006 Map atlas classes to a published outcome taxonomy

- **Question:** Can each atlas class be placed under a domain of the Dodd et al. 2018 outcome taxonomy, and which classes fit none?
- **Why it matters:** A shared taxonomy lets others compare the atlas with outcome work in other conditions.
- **Sources:**
  - T1, literature, read 2026-10-10. Dodd et al. 2018, a taxonomy of outcome domains, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5854263/: The controlling agent read the abstract page text: 38 outcome domains in five core areas; it says registry outcomes "can be entered as free text only".
  - T0, literature, not read by us. a report that mapping outcome concepts to UMLS covered only part of them, found in the 2026-10-10 literature search; citation to be recorded: Agent-read: about 44 percent of outcome concepts covered. T0 here.
- **Data:** clinicaltrials-gov, europe-pmc (api); already have: no; fields missing: the taxonomy's domain list, read from the open-access article
- **Effort:** M (estimate)
- **Guard:** open-access-quote, lab-position. Domain names come from the open-access article under its licence; each mapping is a lab position until a person reviews it.
- **Must not claim:**
  - That the mapping is endorsed by the taxonomy's authors.
  - That a class that fits no domain is a gap in CF research.
- **Needs a person:** clinician-reader
- **Links:** none
- **Recorded:** created 2026-10-10 by model (claude-opus-5-5); updated 2026-10-10

- **Needs a person:** maintainer-approval
- **Links:** none

- **Not in the catalog:** COMET database

### L-0016 A measured, quote-verified classifier for registry primary outcomes

- **Question:** How well does the atlas's quote-verified classifier agree with a frozen, person-labelled set of primary outcomes?
- **Why it matters:** A published agreement measure would let other groups judge whether such a classifier is fit for their own use.
- **Sources:**
  - T0, literature, not read by us. a quick literature search, 2026-10-10: No published evaluation of a registry primary-outcome classifier with agreement numbers was found; an empty search is not proof of absence.
  - T0, run, not read by us. trial atlas, first real run, blind challenger, 2026-10-10: The challenger agreed on 84 percent of 150 sampled entries (95 percent interval 77 to 89); agreement is not correctness.
- **Data:** clinicaltrials-gov (api); already have: yes; fields missing: a frozen labelled set
- **Effort:** M (estimate)
- **Guard:** computed, lab-position. A methods note only after the frozen set is measured; all agreement figures are computed with their intervals.
- **Must not claim:**
  - That the classifier is accurate on the strength of model-to-model agreement.
  - That no such classifier has been published.
- **Needs a person:** clinician-reader, maintainer-approval
- **Links:** board T-0130
- **Recorded:** created 2026-10-10 by model (claude-opus-5-5); updated 2026-10-10

## Data-available

### L-0003 How differently trials define pulmonary exacerbation, FEV1 and sweat chloride outcomes

- **Question:** How many distinct definitions do CF trials register for pulmonary exacerbation, FEV1 and sweat chloride outcomes, counted by rule facets such as time frame and threshold?
- **Why it matters:** Outcomes defined in different ways are hard to compare across trials, and a count of the definitions shows where comparison needs care.
- **Sources:**
  - T0, literature, not read by us. a systematic review of outcomes in 144 CF studies, found in the 2026-10-10 literature search; citation to be recorded: Agent-read abstract: it reported "a wide range of outcomes and corresponding endpoints".
  - T0, council, not read by us. three blind council reviews of the atlas, 2026-10-10
- **Data:** clinicaltrials-gov (api); already have: yes; fields missing: none
- **Effort:** M (estimate)
- **Guard:** computed, registry-statement-verbatim. Counts of definitions by facet are computed; a definition shown is the registry text, quoted verbatim.
- **Must not claim:**
  - That one definition is better or worse than another.
  - That heterogeneity means a trial was badly designed.
- **Needs a person:** clinician-reader
- **Links:** board T-0130
- **Recorded:** created 2026-10-10 by model (claude-opus-5-5); updated 2026-10-10

### L-0007 Trials per class, deduplicated by lead sponsor

- **Question:** How many distinct lead sponsors register trials in each atlas class, once spelling variants of one sponsor are merged by an alias table?
- **Why it matters:** A sponsor count shows whether a class rests on many groups or a few, without ranking anyone.
- **Sources:**
  - T0, council, not read by us. three blind council reviews of the atlas, 2026-10-10: The reviews advised against a network graph, which reads as a ranking.
- **Data:** clinicaltrials-gov (api); already have: yes; fields missing: an alias table for sponsor names (lab-made)
- **Effort:** S (estimate)
- **Guard:** computed, registry-statement-verbatim. Counts are computed; sponsor names are as the registry records them, and every alias merge is listed.
- **Must not claim:**
  - A ranking of sponsors or any judgement of a sponsor.
  - That a sponsor's count reflects its contribution to CF care.
- **Needs a person:** maintainer-approval
- **Links:** board T-0130
- **Recorded:** created 2026-10-10 by model (claude-opus-5-5); updated 2026-10-10

- **Effort:** S (estimate)
- **Guard:** computed, registry-statement-verbatim. The share is computed from the snapshot; the bulletin is quoted verbatim; the cause stays an inference.
- **Must not claim:**
  - Why older records lack the date type, beyond what the registry states.
  - That records without a date type are wrong.
- **Needs a person:** none
- **Links:** board T-0130
- **Recorded:** created 2026-10-10 by model (claude-opus-5-5); updated 2026-10-10

## Done

### L-0001 Unsorted remainder of the trial atlas, sorted by a local model with exact-quote checks

- **Question:** Can a local model propose a class for the primary outcomes the atlas lexicon leaves unsorted, with every proposal backed by an exact quote from the registry record?
- **Why it matters:** Without it, a large unsorted remainder would hide part of what CF trials register as their main outcome.
- **Sources:**
  - T0, run, not read by us. trial atlas route, first real runs (board T-0130): Done in the atlas route; the tools are in pull request cf-research#39. A verified quote proves only that the words exist in the record.
- **Data:** clinicaltrials-gov (api); already have: yes; fields missing: none
- **Effort:** M (estimate)
- **Guard:** computed, registry-statement-verbatim. Counts are computed from the snapshot; any registry text shown is quoted verbatim and checked against the record.
- **Must not claim:**
  - That a model's class for an outcome is correct because its quote was found in the record.
  - That the atlas classes measure trial quality.
- **Needs a person:** maintainer-approval
- **Links:** board T-0130; pull requests cf-research#39; proposals proposals/2026-10-10-trial-endpoint-atlas.md
- **Recorded:** created 2026-10-10 by model (claude-opus-5-5); updated 2026-10-10
